annotations.title: 迪化
annotations.body: 迪化，即今烏魯木齊，為清代新疆重鎮。乾隆朝兩度用兵準噶爾，平定天山南北，展拓西北疆域，並在此設治屯戍。乾隆帝屢言「中外一家」，以天下一家之說統攝內地與藩部，將新疆納入大一統版圖。

zh-Hans.title: 迪化
zh-Hans.body: 迪化，即今乌鲁木齐，为清代新疆重镇。乾隆朝两度用兵准噶尔，平定天山南北，展拓西北疆域，并在此设治屯戍。乾隆帝屡言「中外一家」，以天下一家之说统摄内地与藩部，将新疆纳入大一统版图。

en.title: Dihua
en.body: Dihua (today's Ürümqi) was a key Qing stronghold in Xinjiang. Under the Qianlong emperor, two campaigns against the Dzungars pacified both sides of the Tianshan, expanded the northwest frontier, and established administration and military colonies here. Qianlong often spoke of "one family within and beyond," folding Xinjiang into a unified imperial map of the inner lands and outer dependencies.

annotations.title: 題識
annotations.body:
本朝幅員之廣亘古未有東西南朔莫不紀極而萬國之梯航重譯職貢稱臣者更指不勝屈乾隆
      丁亥年間餘姚黃千人曾為天下輿圖其中山川疆界都邑封圻靡不星羅棋布如指諸掌洵足瞻
盛世之版章為遠近之觀度矣然其時金川西藏新疆州郡未經開闢而河道海口等尚不無挂漏之說
      兹刻遵      御纂諸書悉為增補較舊圖似加詳晰全圖內每方百里凡省■̅府從□廳從▮直隸
      州從⌂州從■縣從●關從⏠營鎮從◎土司從▲其塞徼緜亘無際海峙風設不時雜以里數計
      者其方向俱仍舊式未敢稍易己見舊圖勒石不便攜帶屏幅途寓中玩鑒已加整正博雅君子
      使歸全壁之懸覽幸焉
   嘉慶十有七年歲在壬申桂月上浣吉旦

zh-Hans.title: 题识
zh-Hans.body:
本朝幅员之广亘古未有，东西南朔莫不纪极，而万国之梯航重译、职贡称臣者更指不胜屈。乾隆丁亥年间，余姚黄千人曾为天下舆图，其中山川疆界、都邑封圻靡不星罗棋布、如指诸掌，洵足瞻盛世之版章，为远近之观度矣。然其时金川、西藏、新疆州郡未经开辟，而河道海口等尚不无挂漏之说。兹刻遵      御纂诸书悉为增补，较旧图似加详晰。全图内每方百里；凡省■̅，府从□，厅从▮，直隶州从⌂，州从■，县从●，关从⏠，营镇从◎，土司从▲。其塞徼绵亘无际、海峙风设不时、杂以里数计者，其方向俱仍旧式，未敢稍易己见。旧图勒石不便携带，屏幅途寓中玩鉴已加整正，博雅君子使归全壁之悬览幸焉。
嘉庆十有七年岁在壬申桂月上浣吉旦
（以上为题识原文的现代标点整理；图例符号与御字前空格仍依原刻。）

en.title: Colophon
en.body:
A Jiaqing-era colophon (1812) praises the empire’s unprecedented breadth, and the realms that come by ship and interpreter to offer tribute and acknowledge the throne — more than the fingers can count. It recalls Huang Qianren of Yuyao and his world map of 1767 (Qianlong dinghai): mountains, rivers, boundaries, and seats laid out like points on the palm, truly enough to behold the territorial order of a flourishing age. Jinchuan, Tibet, and the prefectures of Xinjiang had not yet been opened then, and rivers and harbors still had gaps. This engraving follows the imperially commissioned compilations and fills those in, somewhat more fully than the older plate. Each square is one hundred li. The legend marks a province with ■̅, a prefecture (fu) with □, a subprefecture (ting) with ▮, a directly administered department with ⌂, a department (zhou) with ■, a county with ●, a pass with ⏠, a garrison town with ◎, and a tusi with ▲. Where the frontier marches stretch on without end, or sea and wind leave the measure unsettled, distances in li are still given and the old bearings are kept; I have not dared to alter my own view of them in the slightest. The older map was cut in stone and awkward to carry. This screen copy has been set right for viewing on the road and in lodgings, so that learned readers may hang the whole piece and look at it — that would be a kindness.
Dated the first decade of the eighth lunar month, Jiaqing 17 (rénshēn).

zh-Hans.title: 朝鲜
zh-Hans.body: 朝鲜，古箕子国。汉置元菟、乐浪二郡，后隋入高丽，唐置安东都护府，自后历代朝贡。本朝封朝鲜国王。其地东西南濒海，北抵长白山，东西二千里，南北四千里。由国城过鸭绿江至京师三千五百里。京畿道领郡三、府三、州七、县三；江源道领郡七、府五、州四、县十；黄海道领郡三、府三、州五、县八；全罗道领郡三、府三、州四、县二十三；庆尚道领郡七、府六、州五、县十一；忠清道领郡四、州九、县七；咸镜道领郡三、府五、州八；平安道领郡十一、府九、州十六、县六。

en.title: Korea
en.body: Korea, the ancient realm of Jizi. Han established the commanderies of Xuantu and Lelang; it later passed into Goguryeo, and Tang set up the Andong Protectorate. Tribute continued under the dynasties that followed. This dynasty invests the king of Joseon. The land meets the sea on the east, west, and south, and Changbai Mountain on the north: two thousand li east to west, four thousand north to south. From the royal city across the Yalu to the capital is 3,500 li. The eight provinces and their commanderies, prefectures, departments, and counties are then listed.

en.title: Altan River
en.body: The Yellow River issues east of Bayan Har, in the western fan lands, and is named the Altan. It flows northeast three hundred li and more, joining the springs of Odontala, hundreds and thousands of pools large and small strewn in rows like stars. They gather into the two lakes Zhaling and Eling; each is three hundred li and more around, fifty li from east to west. The river turns north, passes south of Mongol Tuoluhai Mountain, then southeast for a thousand li and more. It takes in several dozen lesser streams from north and south, passes below Ulan Mangnai, and is joined from the southeast by the Domodatkun Dolon and the Dolakun Dolon. From there it turns and flows north three hundred li and more. Lesser streams rush in beyond counting. It bends east of Mount Amnyemaqen, runs a hundred and fifty li, and receives the Qipu and the Huhusu from the west. It continues northeast three hundred li and more, meets the Haketu and the streams that follow, passes Guide fortress and Jishi Mountain, and at Lanzhou, at Hezhou, enters China.

zh-Hans.title: 西天
zh-Hans.body: 西天，即汉身毒国。按馆考云：西天即天竺，在葱岭之南，去月氏底东南数千里，地方三万余里，分东西南北中五印度国，各有王，地皆数千里。

en.title: India
en.body: The Western Heaven is the Shendu of the Han. A gazetteer says it is Tianzhu, south of the Congling, several thousand li southeast of the Yuezhi, more than thirty thousand li across, divided into the five Indias — east, west, south, north, and center — each with its own king and a territory of several thousand li.

annotations.title: 河源
annotations.body:
元潘昂霄河源志曰
吐蕃朵甘思西部有
泉百餘泓方可七八
十里履高下瞰燦若
列星故名火敦腦兒
華言星宿也宋
思本云河源在中州
西南直四川馬湖蠻
部之正西三千餘里
雲南麗江宣撫司之
西北一千五百餘里

zh-Hans.title: 河源
zh-Hans.body: 元潘昂霄《河源志》曰：吐蕃朵甘思西部有泉百余泓，方可七八十里，履高下瞰，灿若列星，故名火敦脑儿，华言星宿也。宋思本云：河源在中州西南，直四川马湖蛮部之正西三千余里，云南丽江宣抚司之西北一千五百余里。

en.title: Source of the Yellow River
en.body: Pan Angxiao’s Yuan treatise on the river source says that in the west of Dokham in Tibet more than a hundred springs spread over seventy or eighty li. Seen from above they glitter like stars, hence Huodun Nao’er, “Starry Lake” in Chinese. Zhu Siben says the source lies southwest of the central provinces, three thousand li due west of the Mahu country in Sichuan, and 1,500 li northwest of the Lijiang pacification office in Yunnan.

zh-Hans.title: 安南
zh-Hans.body: 安南国，本古南交地。秦象郡，汉交趾、九真、日南三郡。地甚广，东西相距一千七百里，南北二千八百里。唐曰交州，后改为安南都护府。宋封安南王。明初改交趾布政司。本朝封安南国王，每岁朝贡。入交有三道：由广东、由广西、由云南。一由广东之钦州，一由广西之思明府，一由云南之蒙自。

en.title: Annam
en.body: Annam, the ancient Nanjao. Qin’s Xiang commandery; Han’s Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, and Rinan. About 1,700 li east to west and 2,800 north to south. Tang called it Jiaozhou, later the Annan Protectorate. Song invested a king of Annam. Early Ming made it the Jiaozhi administration. This dynasty invests the king of Annam, who sends tribute every year. Three roads lead in: from Qinzhou in Guangdong, Siming in Guangxi, and Mengzi in Yunnan.

annotations.title: 日本
annotations.body:
日本古倭奴國唐始改名其地
在會稽之東近海由寧波入分五畿七道
      三島附庸之國九百餘島

zh-Hans.title: 日本
zh-Hans.body: 日本，古倭奴国，唐始改名。其地在会稽之东，近海，由宁波入。分五畿七道、三岛，附庸之国九百余岛。

en.title: Japan
en.body: Japan, the ancient land of Wo. Tang first gave it this name. It lies east of Kuaiji, close to the sea, and is reached from Ningbo. It is divided into five capital provinces, seven circuits, and three islands, with more than nine hundred dependent islands.

annotations.title: 俄羅斯
annotations.body:
俄羅斯東連羅剎迤西直北俱其地界
謹按平定羅剎方略云俄羅斯自額濟勒
河東至大洋北至北海西至國界其國距
京師甚遠由此陸路可直達彼處自嘉峪
關行十三日至哈密自哈密行十二三日
至吐魯番過土魯番五種部落即俄羅斯
之境其國遼闊有一萬餘里

zh-Hans.title: 俄罗斯
zh-Hans.body: 俄罗斯，东连罗刹，迤西直北俱其地界。谨按《平定罗刹方略》云：俄罗斯自额济勒河东至大洋，北至北海，西至国界。其国距京师甚远，由此陆路可直达彼处。自嘉峪关行十三日至哈密，自哈密行十二三日至吐鲁番。过吐鲁番五种部落，即俄罗斯之境。其国辽阔，有一万余里。

en.title: Russia
en.body: Russia joins the Luocha on the east; west and due north are all its bounds. The Official Account of the Pacification of the Luocha says Russia runs from the Volga east to the ocean, north to the northern sea, and west to its own frontier. The country is very far from the capital, but a land road reaches it: thirteen days from Jiayu Pass to Hami, twelve or thirteen more to Turpan. Beyond Turpan’s five tribes is Russian ground. The realm is vast, more than ten thousand li across.

en.title: Taiwan
en.body: Eastward, all is indigenous territory, and no track reaches it. The prefecture runs 2,840 li from north to south. Fifty li to the east is the indigenous boundary at Huoshan.

en.title: Holland
en.body: Holland lies north of the western sea. The Zhengzhi Dianxun says that Holland borders Russia, and that their languages are mutually intelligible.

en.title: Altai Mountains
en.body: The Altai: the name means Gold Mountain. The Personal Campaigns to Pacify the Desert says that the northwestern Gold Mountain lies about two months' journey to the west of here, and that it is the ancient kingdom of Dayuan.
